title: Cold rebuild: Find vulnerable dependencies
summary: Rebuild Find vulnerable dependencies from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Find vulnerable dependencies** in *Dependencies, SBOMs and pinned actions*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Nobody changed the repo for three months, yet the nightly pipeline started failing its vulnerability gate. Why?
options: A new advisory was published for a package version you already use
steps.explain: Vulnerability data changes daily. That is why scans run on a schedule, not only on code changes.

steps.title: Rebuild Find vulnerable dependencies cold
prompt: Write `List<string> Vulnerable(Dictionary<string, string> installed, List<(string Package, string FixedIn)> advisories)`.
A package is vulnerable when it is installed at a version **older** than `FixedIn` (plain `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, compared numerically).
Return lines like `"System.Text.Json 8.0.4 -> 8.0.5"`, sorted ordinally, without duplicates. A helper method `IsOlder` is a good idea.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<string> Vulnerable(Dictionary<string, string> installed, List<(string Package, string FixedIn)> advisories)
